Custom integrations by **[seb5594](https://github.com/seb5594)**, in one place.
Browse by the name you see in Home Assistant, check each project's status, and install what you need.

---

## Install

**Individual integration:** use its **Open in HACS** link below. HACS manages that integration's updates directly.

**One repository to discover them all:** add this repository to HACS as an **Integration**, download it, and restart Home Assistant. Under **Settings → Devices & services**, select **Configure** on the discovered **seb5594's Integration Hub** card. By default, the hub automatically adds the catalog's individual repositories to HACS and notifies you when new integrations appear.

Discovery uses the local Home Assistant mDNS announcement (Zeroconf, enabled by default). If unavailable, use **Add integration** and search for the hub.

[![Open catalog in HACS](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/hacs_repository.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/hacs_repository/?owner=seb5594&repository=Home-Assistant-Integrations&category=integration)

**HACS manages each integration's downloads and updates normally.** The hub adds repository URLs; it does not automatically download, configure or restart anything. Catalog-only changes never bump the hub version or publish a hub release. Its hourly catalog check detects newly listed projects without requiring a hub update and sends a Home Assistant notification with friendly names and HACS links. The first check establishes a baseline; existing entries are not announced as new.

Automatic registration uses HACS' internal runtime registry and is **experimental**. If the API is unavailable, direct HACS links remain available and the hub retries. Both automatic registration and notifications can be disabled under **Configure → Hub settings**. A **Refresh catalog** button checks immediately. No HACS storage file is edited directly.

**Home Assistant compatibility:** the hub supports **2024.1.2 or newer**, with CI coverage for 2024.1.2, 2024.12.4, 2025.1.0, 2025.12.4 and 2026.10.4. Individual catalog integrations retain their own minimum versions. [Compatibility details](docs/INSTALL.md#compatibility).

**HACS → Marketplace:** HA 2026.11.0 and later require the new store; actual Marketplace detection also handles early installations. The hub checks readiness and API capabilities before writing repository metadata. [Transition policy and diagnostics](docs/HACS-MARKETPLACE.md).

**Release packages only:** the catalog uses GitHub's latest published non-draft, non-prerelease release for each project. Version labels link to that exact tag, and package links point to its uploaded integration ZIP. Projects without a published release package are omitted until one is available. HACS remains the only installer and update manager.

**[🇬🇧 Installation, updates and removal →](docs/INSTALL.md)** · **[🇩🇪 Deutsche Anleitung →](docs/INSTALL.de.md)** · [HACS repository requirements](https://www.hacs.dev/docs/publish/integration/)

## Source organization

```text
integrations/                         Original repositories, one pinned submodule per integration
custom_components/seb5594_integration_catalog/
  catalog.json                        Latest release tags, package URLs and release commit pins
  hub.py                              Hourly discovery and deduplicated HA notifications
  hacs_bridge.py                      Capability-checked HACS repository registration
  config_flow.py                      Repository and notification settings
catalog-feed.json                     Lightweight public discovery feed
assets/brands/                        Source project logos and attribution
docs/                                 Installation and maintenance notes
scripts/sync_catalog.py               Public-source discovery and catalog generation
templates/README.md                   Editable source of this page
```

Submodules are for browsing and development. Users do not need Git or a recursive clone to use the hub.
To work on the sources locally, run `git submodule update --init --recursive` after cloning this repository.

## Support

For a device or integration problem, open an issue in that integration's source repository linked above.
For catalog discovery, installation or backup problems, [open an issue here](https://github.com/seb5594/Home-Assistant-Integrations/issues).

## Say thanks

All my projects are built in my spare time, just for the fun of it. Still, they take a lot of time and care, and many of the smart home gadgets I buy end up here because I want to make them cloud-free and smart-home ready. Every bit of support means a lot to me.

If my work helped you or turned out to be useful, show your appreciation with a hot drink for my next sleepless night.
